# Salesforce schema

<!-- Generated by `npm run generate-sf-docs`. Edit lib/salesforce/mapping.ts instead. -->

Artificer writes two related records on approval: a `Property__c` and an
`Opportunity` that looks up to it.

## Where these names come from

They were derived from the public API behind nnnpro.com
(`api.surmount.com/sf-opportunities`), which serves a Salesforce replica —
every record carries a `salesforce_id`, and the replica nests an `sf_property`
inside each opportunity. The replica's snake_case columns map back to
Salesforce API names by the usual convention.

The strongest evidence is `x1031_exchange`: Salesforce prefixes an `X` to any
API name that would otherwise start with a digit, so that column can only have
come from `X1031_Exchange__c`. Standard Opportunity fields corroborate it —
`stage_name` ← `StageName`, `close_date` ← `CloseDate`.

Each field below records its origin:

| Origin | Meaning |
| --- | --- |
| **observed** | The replica column was seen on the live API; the API name follows from it. |
| **standard** | A standard Salesforce field, corroborated by the replica. |
| **proposed** | Artificer extracts this but no matching field was observed. Create it, or drop the mapping. |

> Casing caveat: snake_case is lossy, so `Building_Size_SF__c` could be
> `Building_Size_Sf__c` in the org. Salesforce resolves field names
> case-insensitively, so this is a cosmetic risk rather than a breaking one.

## Property__c — Property

| Field | API name | Replica column | Origin | From |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Property Name | `Name` | — | standard | _derived_ |
| Street | `Property_Address_Street__c` | `property_address_street` | observed | `property.streetAddress` |
| City | `Property_Address_City__c` | `property_address_city` | observed | `property.city` |
| State | `Property_Address_State__c` | `property_address_state` | observed | `property.state` |
| Postal Code | `Property_Address_Postal_Code__c` | `property_address_postal_code` | observed | `property.zip` |
| Property Type | `Property_Type__c` | `property_type` | observed | `property.propertyType` |
| Building Size (SF) | `Building_Size_SF__c` | `building_size_sf` | observed | `property.buildingSf` |
| Lot Size (acres) | `Lot_Size_AC__c` | `lot_size_ac` | observed | `property.lotSizeAcres` |
| Year Built | `Year_Built__c` | `year_built` | observed | `property.yearBuilt` |
| Concept | `Concept__c` | `concept` | observed | `tenant.tradeName` |
| Credit Type | `Credit_Type__c` | `credit_type` | observed | `tenant.guarantorType` |
| Renewal Options | `Renewal_Options_Remaining__c` | `renewal_options_remaining` | observed | `lease.renewalOptions` |
| Landlord Responsibility | `Landlord_Responsibility__c` | `landlord_responsibility` | observed | `lease.landlordResponsibilities` |
| Tenant Legal Entity | `Tenant_Legal_Entity__c` | — | proposed | `tenant.legalEntityName` |
| Guarantor | `Guarantor_Name__c` | — | proposed | `tenant.guarantorName` |
| Credit Rating | `Credit_Rating__c` | — | proposed | `tenant.creditRating` |

- **`Property_Address_State__c`** — Drives the State filter on the public site.
- **`Property_Type__c`** — Picklist. Options are served publicly at /sf-opportunities/public/visible-property-types.
- **`Concept__c`** — Picklist. Options are served at /sf-opportunities/public/property-dropdown-options/concept, and it drives the Concept filter — a free-text value would produce a listing no filter can find.
- **`Credit_Type__c`** — Artificer's guarantor classification (corporate / franchisee / personal / none) is the closest match; the org's picklist values should be confirmed.
- **`Tenant_Legal_Entity__c`** — The signing entity is not exposed publicly, but it is what a buyer underwrites.

## Opportunity — Opportunity (listing)

| Field | API name | Replica column | Origin | From |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Opportunity Name | `Name` | `name` | standard | _derived_ |
| Stage | `StageName` | `stage_name` | standard | _derived_ |
| List Price | `List_Price__c` | `list_price` | observed | `economics.askingPrice` |
| List NOI | `List_Net_Operating_Income__c` | `list_net_operating_income` | observed | `economics.annualBaseRent` |
| Lease Type | `Lease_Type__c` | `lease_type` | observed | `lease.leaseType` |
| Lease Commencement | `Lease_Commencement__c` | `lease_commencement` | observed | `lease.commencementDate` |
| Lease Expiration | `Lease_Expiration__c` | `lease_expiration` | observed | `lease.expirationDate` |
| Lease Term Remaining | `Lease_Term_Remaining__c` | `lease_term_remaining` | observed | `lease.remainingTermYears` |
| Rental Increases | `Rental_Increases__c` | `rental_increases` | observed | `lease.rentEscalations` |
| Description | `Description__c` | `description` | standard | _derived_ |
| Artificer Deal Id | `Artificer_Deal_Id__c` | — | proposed | _derived_ |
| Deal Hash | `Deal_Hash__c` | — | proposed | _derived_ |

- **`StageName`** — Artificer writes an early-funnel stage; a deal reaching the public site is a later, human decision.
- **`Artificer_Deal_Id__c`** — Links the CRM record back to the reviewed deal and its audit trail.
- **`Deal_Hash__c`** — External ID + Unique. This is what makes re-approval idempotent.

## Relationship

```
Property__c  <──lookup──  Opportunity
```

`Property__c` is written first, because the Opportunity's lookup needs its id.

## Fields Artificer extracts but does not write

| Field | Why |
| --- | --- |
| Cap Rate (`economics.capRate`) | Derived downstream from list price and NOI. |
| Price / SF (`economics.pricePerSf`) | Derived downstream from list price and building size. |

These are still extracted, cited and reviewed — a reviewer should check a
stated cap rate against price and NOI, and a mismatch is worth catching. They
are simply not written, because the listing derives them.

## Org changes required

5 fields below were not observed on the public model and must be created:

| Object | API name | Type | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `Property__c` | `Tenant_Legal_Entity__c` | Text | The signing entity is not exposed publicly, but it is what a buyer underwrites. |
| `Property__c` | `Guarantor_Name__c` | Text |  |
| `Property__c` | `Credit_Rating__c` | Text |  |
| `Opportunity` | `Artificer_Deal_Id__c` | Text | Links the CRM record back to the reviewed deal and its audit trail. |
| `Opportunity` | `Deal_Hash__c` | Text | External ID + Unique. This is what makes re-approval idempotent. |

`Deal_Hash__c` must be marked **External ID** and **Unique** — it is what makes
re-approval update the existing records instead of creating duplicates.

## Picklists

Two fields are picklist-backed on the public site, and their options are served
publicly:

```
GET /sf-opportunities/public/property-dropdown-options/concept
GET /sf-opportunities/public/visible-property-types
```

`Concept__c` matters most: it drives the Concept filter on the marketplace, so a
free-text value produces a listing that no filter can find. Artificer currently
extracts the tenant trade name as free text. Validating it against the live
picklist at extraction time is the single highest-value change to make next.

## Switching to a real org

```
SF_LOGIN_URL=https://login.salesforce.com   # or test.salesforce.com for a sandbox
SF_USERNAME=integration@example.com
SF_PASSWORD=<password><security token>      # concatenated, no separator
SF_INSTANCE_URL=https://your-domain.my.salesforce.com   # optional, enables link-out
```

All three of the first are required together; a partial configuration
deliberately falls back to mock rather than failing at the moment of approval.

Because the marketplace reads from a Salesforce replica, writing here *is*
publishing — an approved deal reaches nnnpro.com through the sync that already
exists. That is precisely why the approval gate sits where it does.
